title: QuickFilter — The URL Never Leaves the Browser
objective: The dashboard highlights a 'quick filter' straight from the page's own URL — no page reload, no server round trip. Make the admin's browser run your script when they open a link you send them.

verifier.condition: The payload exfiltrates the admin-only data-token rendered on /dashboard, proving it executed inside an authenticated admin session reached via a URL fragment the server never sees.

weakness: Client-side JavaScript reads the URL fragment and writes it into the page with innerHTML, with no server round trip and no sanitization, so a crafted fragment runs as script in the viewer's browser.
vulnerableEndpoint: GET /dashboard#filter=<payload> (read by client-side JS, never sent to the server)
seededData: One admin session (minted by the lab's own admin-bot endpoint) with a per-instance token rendered only for admins. In-memory.
hints: This page never seems to send your filter text anywhere, yet it visibly reacts to it. Where could that logic live?
The browser never sends a URL's fragment (everything after #) to the server at all. If the page still responds to it, something in the page itself must be reading it.
Look at how the active filter gets drawn onto the page. Is it built as text, or inserted as markup?
burpNotes: Burp never sees the fragment either — it isn't sent in any request. Use 'Simulate admin visit' with a path like /dashboard#filter=<payload> to test this one; it fires client-side the moment the page loads for the admin bot.
